title: pennsylvania-lpm Coherence-Analysis Finding Record
description: One empirical finding from directly reading official Pennsylvania science-standards or court-record documents: a gap, a working cross-reference, a wording change between editions, or a divergence between what a school district mandated and what the state's own standards actually require. The computable unit underneath prose in docs/source-notes/ -- lets a query ask 'which adopted mandates (institutional-mandate-record) have a supporting or contradicting finding' and 'did Dover Area School District's 2004 policy go further than anything in Pennsylvania's own state science standards ever required'. Modeled on deutsche_lp's/nys_lp's/india-lpm's/florida-lpm's coherence-finding-record.schema.json; findingType is adapted since Pennsylvania's defining pattern is NOT a single state authority re-adopting the same standard across decades (contrast florida-lpm) -- it is a three-level story (a single school district's own policy, the state's separate standards, and a federal court ruling that bound neither directly but shaped both going forward).

findingType.description: 'uncrossreferenced-gap' = no link found between related content in two policy objects that would benefit from one. 'working-crossreference' = a real cross-reference was found and confirmed. 'standard-wording-change-across-editions' = a finding about how a specific benchmark's own wording changed between two named editions of Pennsylvania's own state science standards -- a fact about the policy text's own evolution, not about external curriculum. 'standard-naming-explicitness-gap' = whether a given edition names a contested concept (e.g. 'evolution', 'natural selection', 'climate change') explicitly at all, versus using vaguer or substitute language, versus omitting it entirely. 'district-vs-state-standard-divergence' = a finding about how a specific school district's own curriculum mandate (e.g. Dover Area School District's 2004 policy) compared to what Pennsylvania's own state-level standards actually required at the same time -- distinct from a cross-EDITION comparison, this is a cross-LEVEL comparison within the same jurisdiction. 'litigation-finding-vs-standard-text' = whether a specific factual or legal finding from a court ruling (e.g. a Kitzmiller v. Dover finding about what intelligent design is or isn't) is reflected, contradicted, or simply absent in subsequent official standards text. 'convergent-coverage-pattern' = 2+ independent sources (official text, a textbook, a state resource page) converge on the same content emphasis. 'cross-state-standards-divergence' = comparison with another state's (Florida via florida-lpm, New York via nys_lp, or any state covered in national_ccs_policy/) equivalent standard or episode.

objects.description: The policy object(s) this finding is about. One object alone is valid for a single-source placement fact that a later finding might compare against; most findings compare 2+ (e.g. the same benchmark across two editions).

policyArea.description: e.g. 'Dover Area School District's intelligent-design disclaimer statement', 'Pennsylvania Academic Standards for Science and Technology, biological evolution benchmarks', 'Kitzmiller v. Dover ruling, Establishment Clause findings'.

excerptText.description: A short verbatim excerpt grounding the object, where one exists in the source doc.

accessTier.description: How much of this object's source document this record actually keeps in excerptText, chosen per-source based on what's legally safe to redistribute for this document -- not one all-or-nothing repo-wide rule. Identical field to deutsche_lp's/nys_lp's/india-lpm's coherence-finding-record.schema.json.

licenseOrRightsNote.description: The legal basis for storing excerptText at the accessTier chosen above. Mirrors OpenLPM's standards_documents.license_or_rights_note field (openlpm migration 019) for ecosystem-wide naming consistency.

summary.description: One or two sentences stating the finding in plain language -- what was found, not why it matters (see policyRelevance for that).

policyRelevance.description: Optional: why this finding matters for curriculum policy or for OpenEvo's own strategy, if not already obvious from summary.

testsMandateIds.description: Institutional-mandate-record ids this finding provides evidence for, against, or relevant to.

relatedControversyIds.description: policy-controversy-record ids this finding provides direct textual evidence for -- e.g. a wording-change finding that documents exactly what a controversy's contestedObjects fight was actually about.

themes.description: Which content theme(s) this finding is evidentially about -- kept as an open, non-enum string list since this repo's theme taxonomy has not yet stabilized.

exhaustivenessCaveat.description: Explicit statement of how exhaustive the underlying search was, e.g. 'based on the specific editions and benchmark codes fetched this session, not a systematic benchmark-by-benchmark diff of every life-science standard across all four editions' -- required honesty; omit only when a search genuinely was exhaustive (rare).
